versions.name: RXV2-0.9.305-every-page-teaches-time
versions.notes: Every page now teaches the receiver the time, and the Black box page re-teaches it the moment it notices the clock is unset - so sitting on one screen through a receiver reboot no longer leaves it ignorant of the date until you happen to navigate. One shared, rate-limited helper replaces the per-page copies.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.304-field-telemetry
versions.notes: Field fix from today's three test flights: after landing away from home WiFi, the receiver kept the flight controller cut off during its ~2 minutes of hopeful WiFi retries - so the Black box showed 'no telemetry' with the battery plugged in. The flight-controller line now stays connected throughout, and the battery card fills in seconds at the field, just as it does at home.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.303-help-catches-up
versions.notes: The help screens catch up with reality: flying needs no buttons (transmitter on first and the radios manage themselves - explained on the front page), the flight diary holds twenty dated flights with a delete button and landscape mode, and the Black box help explains the self-tending clocks. Written down so nobody has to remember - not even the author.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.302-phone-teaches-tx
versions.notes: The circle closes: whenever the receiver's clock came from a phone, it now offers that true time back to the transmitter over the radio link (ack item 37) - and the updated transmitter quietly corrects its own drifty clock from it. Most models never carry GPS, but every model meets a phone; now every phone connection keeps the whole fleet's clocks honest. Needs the matching transmitter update.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.301-clock-on-screen
versions.notes: The clock steps on stage: the Black box status card now shows the receiver's date and time and who taught it (phone or transmitter, with the calibration figure), and the current flight's card says when the session started - so you can see at a glance that the timekeeping is alive, not just trust the event log.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.300-clock-calibration
versions.notes: Version 300! The transmitter's clock turned out to show UTC plus six minutes of drift, not local time - never assume. The receiver now calibrates it against the phone whenever both are present (every bench session), remembers the offset, and applies it on phone-free field days. Flight stamps come out right no matter what the transmitter's clock face believes.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.299-param-trace
versions.notes: Detective's notebook: the receiver now logs every kind of parameter packet the transmitter sends, once per power-on - so 'did the time packet even arrive?' is answered by a glance at the event log. Pairs with a transmitter update that re-sends its clock every minute instead of trusting one fragile moment at connect.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.298-clock-candour
versions.notes: The transmitter-clock feature now narrates itself: every time packet from the TX is logged with its fate - applied ('Clock set by TX'), outranked ('TX clock heard - phone rules', normal whenever the phone is connected), or rejected with the raw values. No more silent mysteries when testing at the bench.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.297-tx-clock
versions.notes: The transmitter becomes the timekeeper: its battery-backed, GPS-synchronised clock now tells the receiver the time just after every connection - so flights get proper dates even on phone-free field days, and a battery swap no longer wipes the receiver's sense of time. The phone still teaches the timezone (remembered forever) and takes precedence when connected. Requires the matching transmitter update.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.296-dated-flights
versions.notes: Every flight now says when it happened: the Flight analysis card leads with the date and time (learned quietly from your phone's clock each time the app connects), not just the position in the list. Flights saved before the receiver ever knew the time say so honestly.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.295-honest-warnings
versions.notes: No more crying wolf: saving the global governor from the phone cleared its 'unsaved changes' flag only after the flight controller had rebooted and been re-read - leave the page during those ten seconds and it warned you the save was lost when it wasn't. The flag now clears the instant the save is confirmed in flash, and the after-reboot check patiently retries instead of declaring failure on one slow reply.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.294-verified-writes
versions.notes: Trust, but verify: saving settings from the transmitter used to fire commands at the flight controller and hope - and on a busy wire the crucial save-to-memory command could vanish, quietly reverting your edit. Every write is now acknowledged, read back, compared and retried until confirmed; the governor reboot only fires once the save is proven. One press of Save now means exactly one save.
